findings: University of Groningen BA Communication and Information Studies, ISAT 56826, regular English-taught pathway for September 2026 entrants. The Dutch track uses specified Dutch-language modules and a Dutch thesis. The formal redesign gives Year 1 50 EC required and 10 EC chosen from two alternatives. The first listed Humane AI choice is shown using its public course title. Year 2 gives 50 EC required and one 10 EC faculty-wide course. The programme’s curriculum paragraph describes the four themes and confirms a restricted choice. The first-year AI theme continues in Humane AI in Digital Societies: Projects, also listed as 10 EC under LFW001B10 in the faculty course catalog. Year 3 gives a 30 EC minor, two 5 EC advanced communication courses, a 10 EC integrated case study and a 10 EC thesis and research seminar. The prospectus contains older tabular entries alongside newer narrative, so OER Tables 3a, 4a and 5a govern credit-bearing requirements and required courses. Groningen describes the first-semester minor and the second-semester advanced courses, organizational case and thesis. Minor choice, such as study abroad or a placement when approved, remains genuine open curriculum. The required thesis is ordinarily written in English. No separate zero-credit obligation is identified in the programme-specific curriculum.

Table 7a requires Materiality of Communication before Social Media, and Year 1 completion (60 EC), Observing Communication in the Wild and Analysing Communication before the thesis seminar. The Year 1 and Year 2 work precedes those dependent components in this route. The faculty-wide introductory AI course precedes the selected projects course. The older OCASYS thesis course is listed in the transition/current calendar with a shorter prerequisite description, while the explicit September 2026 entrant rules control this cohort.

The closest response combines rhetorical argument and public speaking with stylistics, film/media analysis, social context, qualitative observation and quantitative research. Style & Meaning includes dialogue and turn-taking, and literature and documentary courses bring distinct textual and visual methods. Environmental media and advanced persuasion include evidence-backed sustainability communication. GOSHIST312 contributes question formation, critical source use and a substantial historical paper through its official description. The workplace and health plan connects leadership, negotiation, organizational psychology, inclusion and consumer communication with health consultation, shared decision-making, evidence synthesis and language processing. Psycholinguistics and the prior brain and behavior course can run in the first year, allowing later methods and psychology. Intercultural communication is supported across social theory, cross-cultural negotiation and culturally competent health care rather than a standalone specialist module. The digital plan keeps rhetorical and media analysis at the center and uses programming, text data, learning and neural language models to examine digitally mediated communication. AI ethics supplies fairness, privacy and human agency; media history and digital strategy add technological and institutional context. Introductory rhetoric and Media Archaeology replace Optimization Methods and Organizational Psychology in this plan. This strengthens its communication focus while allowing Deep Learning in the last semester, after Mathematical Methods and Machine Learning. Its courses offer perspectives on human–AI interaction and digital communication, with no dedicated human–computer interaction design sequence. Groningen retains dedicated language, communication intervention design, case study and thesis components. Nine aligned pairs reflect specific shared topics or methods; broader links sit in separate rows. The optional UCR 15 EC research element is outside all schedules and distinct from the compulsory Groningen 10 EC thesis and seminar.
